title: Household Base Rate Usage Bands — Residential Natural Gas Supply Added Premises
content:
**Rule.** For a premise added to a Residential Natural Gas Supply household, the household base rate — the per-therm rate from which the household rate is figured — depends on the home agreement's plan and its recent usage. When the home agreement is on a fixed plan and the therms billed on its energy lines of cycles starting later than the same calendar day twelve months before the enrollment date total 900 or more, the household base rate is the home agreement's contract rate multiplied by 0.97 and rounded half up to four decimal places; when the home agreement is on a fixed plan and those therms total 500 or more but below 900, the household base rate is the home agreement's contract rate minus 0.0100 per therm; in every other case the household base rate is the home agreement's contract rate.

A fixed plan is a plan whose pricing structure is fixed. The usage counted is the therms on the home agreement's energy charge lines whose billing cycle starts after the same calendar day twelve months before the enrollment date.

### Decision table

| Home agreement's plan | Therms on the counted energy lines | Household base rate |
|---|---|---|
| fixed | 900 or more | contract rate multiplied by 0.97, rounded half up to four decimal places |
| fixed | 500 to 899 | contract rate minus 0.0100 |
| fixed | below 500 | contract rate |
| capped variable or variable | any | contract rate |

### Worked cases (hypothetical home agreement, contract rate 0.7480)

- Fixed plan, 960 therms: 0.7480 multiplied by 0.97 is 0.72556, rounded half up to 0.7256.
- Fixed plan, 640 therms: 0.7480 minus 0.0100 is 0.7380.
- Fixed plan, 499 therms: 0.7480.
- Capped variable plan, 1,050 therms: 0.7480.

### The twelve-month window (hypothetical enrollment date 15 October 2025)

An energy line whose cycle starts 16 October 2024 is counted; a line whose cycle starts 15 October 2024 is not.
